review_title: vela atlas 899 feels worse than a simpler stand
review_body_clean: i bought the vela atlas 899 for a shared desk because i wanted my phone held up while i worked. compared with the plain folding stand i had before, this one takes more fiddling and gives me less confidence. the base shifts when i tap the screen, and the viewing angle changes if a cable pulls lightly from the side. its hands-free function operates, but the grip feels weak and the whole accessory seems poorly suited to a busy desk. after several weeks, i avoid placing my phone on it when i need to type, which makes the purchase frustrating rather than helpful. the adjustment joint is the main problem. it moves through a useful range, yet it does not hold that position firmly. i have to tighten it carefully, and even then the phone slowly droops during a video call or while i read a long message. the hinge also makes a rough clicking sound that the simpler stand never made. a wider case leaves the device sitting awkwardly, with one edge close to slipping forward. i expected a compact support to reduce interruptions; instead, i keep reaching over to correct it, and that repeated distraction is disappointing. the atlas is not completely unusable. it can hold a phone on a level surface, and it folds down without much effort, but those basic functions do not outweigh the poor stability. the finish has picked up small marks from ordinary desk use, while the rubber contact areas collect dust and lose their grip. i compared it with two inexpensive stands already in our workspace, and both remain steadier when people share the table. the vela atlas 899 looks more substantial but performs worse where it matters. for hands-free use in a shared workspace, i cannot recommend it and regret choosing it over a simpler design.
